heading: INT. NIGHT BAKERY, BACK KITCHEN - 3 A.M.

units.text: INT. NIGHT BAKERY, BACK KITCHEN - 3 A.M.
Steel tables dusted white.
Proofing racks glow under a single caged bulb.
A radio murmurs a late jazz station.
Flour hangs in the air like weather.
SOLEDAD VEGA, 30s, forearms floured to the elbow, shapes loaves with the speed of someone who has done it ten thousand times.
ARJUN MEHTA, 30s, in a good coat that doesn't belong here, stands at the back door holding a small box he hasn't opened.
BEA LINDGREN, 20s, the new apprentice, sits on an upturned crate peeling a clementine, trying to look invisible.
Door's open. You're letting the heat out.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: I wanted to say, I mean, I came to say
units.name: ARJUN

units.text: I can go. I should go, actually, I have a
units.name: BEA

units.text: Stay, Bea.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: Please, Bea, it's fine. It's
units.name: ARJUN

units.text: It's not fine. It's three in the morning.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: Arjun steps in and shuts the door.
He sets the box on the table beside a tray of rolls, and Soledad slides it two inches away from the dough without looking at it.
Bea tears the clementine in half and offers him a piece, which he takes automatically, which makes Soledad laugh once through her nose.
I kept the key. I'm sorry. I should've mailed it.
units.name: ARJUN

units.text: I'm going to check the oven.
units.name: BEA

units.text: The oven is fine.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: I'm going to check it anyway.
units.name: BEA

units.text: She leaves through the swing door.
It flaps twice behind her.
The radio drops into a slow saxophone.
You cut your hair.
units.name: ARJUN

units.text: Eight months ago.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: It suits you.
units.name: ARJUN

units.text: Don't.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: He opens the box.
Inside is a brass key on a loop of red thread.
He sets it carefully next to the bread, as though it might wake the dough.
She wipes her hands on her apron, one finger at a time, then picks up the key and drops it in the flour bin without looking.
Soledad
units.name: ARJUN

units.text: The seven o'clock rush is in four hours. I've got six hundred rolls.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: Oven's fine!
units.name: BEA

units.text: Told you!
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: Arjun nods, takes a roll off the tray, eats half of it standing there.
Flour dusts his lapel.
He lets it.
Still the best thing in the city.
units.name: ARJUN

units.text: It's flour and water.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: It's you.
units.name: ARJUN

units.text: She takes the other half out of his hand and finishes it herself, chewing slowly, looking at the wall clock.
Then she holds the swing door open for him.
